title: Randomized kernel probing caused intermittent p95 latency spikes
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Short summary: a change that introduced randomized kernel probing in the scheduler increased kernel-switch churn for short-sequence requests, causing cache/tiling inefficiencies and intermittent p95 spikes during mixed workloads. This ticket tracks investigation notes, short-term mitigations, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-28: Alerting flagged a 35% increase in p95 for hosted infer routes serving short-sequence real-time chat; initial blameless pager routed to runtime on-call.
2026-03-01: On-call confirmed correlation with a canary deploy of scheduler v2.7.0 that added randomized kernel probing for path quality estimation.
2026-03-01: Rollback to scheduler v2.6.3 reduced p95 to baseline; incident declared a regression and ownership assigned to serving-runtime team.
2026-03-02: Replayed traces and sampling captured kernel-switch events; observed probe windows coinciding with KV cache misses and increased memory churn for certain batch sizes.
2026-03-04: A/B test of deterministic probing (fixed seed) reproduced lower churn; safety patch prepared to gate randomized probing under mixed-latency SLAs.
2026-03-09: Patch merged to runtime-1.20 branch; rollout staged against low-traffic customer clusters with added telemetry.
2026-03-12: Patch rollout ongoing; ticket opened to convert short-term fix into long-term scheduling heuristics and improved validation.
investigation_summary: We observed that randomized probing added non-deterministic kernel selection for small sequence lengths. The probing heuristic intentionally probes alternate kernel implementations to detect better throughput for unseen workload patterns, but the implementation did not account for KV cache state and prefix reuse. For short sequences (<= 128 tokens), probing often triggered a kernel switch mid-request or between closely related requests which caused cache invalidation and small memory alloc/free cycles in the runtime. This amplified tail latency under mixed traffic when continuous batching produced short-lived batches. Reverting the randomized probe eliminated the spikes, which establishes causality.
root_cause: A scheduler optimization (randomized kernel probing) introduced aggressive probing across incoming requests without respecting request signature affinity or KV cache warmness. The naive probing frequency and lack of affinity hashing led to kernel churn and cache thrash for short, latency-sensitive requests.
action_items: Disable randomized probing by default and gate behind explicit config for experiments (owner: Marco Silva, due: 2026-03-15)
Implement request-signature affinity hashing in the scheduler so probes are grouped by similar prefix/workload (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-04-01)
Add an adaptive probe budget that factors in KV cache warmness and recent kernel-change-rate to avoid probing hot prefixes (owner: Daniel Park, due: 2026-04-08)
Create golden workload tests that include short-sequence chat, embedding-only, and bursty mixed traffic to catch tail regressions in CI (owner: Sofia Chen, due: 2026-03-25)

Surface kernel-switch-rate and kv-cache-miss-by-sequence-length in Console per-route dashboards and create alerts when kernel-change-rate spikes > 3x baseline (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-22)
Backfill telemetry: tag historical traces where kernel switches occurred and compute contribution to p95 for last 90 days (owner: Marco Silva, due: 2026-03-18)

Retention: document a rollback playbook for scheduler experiments and require a canary burn-in of at least 48 hours under production-mixed traffic before enabling non-deterministic probes (owner: Reliability PM, due: 2026-03-20)
Post-deploy: schedule a focused load test simulating 50% short-chat traffic with continuous batching turned on to validate heuristics (owner: SRE, due: 2026-04-05)
Follow-up: evaluate whether quantization-aware kernel selection should prefer stable kernels for latency SLOs (owner: Research/Applied ML, due: 2026-04-15)
acceptance_criteria: Default production scheduler does not enable randomized probing (config off) and p95 for affected routes is within 5% of pre-regression baseline
Kernel-change-rate metric exposed in Console with per-route and per-model breakdowns, and a PagerDuty rule created for >3x sustained increase
Affinity hashing implemented and validated in canary (no tail regressions on golden workloads)
CI includes golden workload regression tests that fail the build if p95 increases by more than configured threshold for short-sequence scenarios
